1	/**
2	 * Session budget guard. Configured token, wall-clock, and cost caps are
3	 * measured against the durable session log before every proposed step; the
4	 * first cap the log exceeds is recorded as a `budget/breach` event, blocks any
5	 * active goal, and rejects the step so no further model request is made. Every
6	 * step served by a priced route also gets a durable `usage/priced` record, so
7	 * session cost replays from the log at the rates that priced it.
8	 *
9	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
10	 */
11	
12	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
14	import type { Agent, PreStepDecision } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
15	// Type-only: resolves ctx.goals for the optional durable block.
16	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
17	import { BUDGET_CAP_ORDER, foldBudgetSpend, foldSessionCaps, measuredFor, tightenedCaps, unpricedUsage } from './fold.ts'
18	import { billedInputTokens, costEurFor, pricingTableDigest, routeKey } from './pricing.ts'
19	import type { AccountedMessage, BudgetBreach, BudgetCapId, BudgetRoutePricing, UsagePriced } from './types.ts'
20	
21	// The pure payload outlet (./types.ts, ONE home of the `budget/caps`,
22	// `budget/breach`, and `usage/priced` declarations) re-exported onto the
23	// package root keeps the module edge in the emitted index.d.ts, so aggregate
24	// programs consuming the declarations still receive the SessionEventMap merge.
25	export type * from './types.ts'
26	export {
27	  BUDGET_CAP_ORDER,
28	  foldBudgetSpend,
29	  foldSessionCaps,
30	  measuredFor,
31	  tightenedCaps,
32	  unpricedUsage,
33	} from './fold.ts'
34	export { pricingTableDigest } from './pricing.ts'

36	/** Cordis plugin name used by loader diagnostics. */

40	export const inject = ['agents']

42	/**
43	 * The block reason this policy writes onto a goal it stops. Stable and
44	 * machine-routable: a supervisor reads it to tell an exhausted budget apart
45	 * from every other blocked goal.
46	 */
47	export const BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = 'budget-exhausted'

49	/**
50	 * Per-session ceilings. Every cap is optional and uncapped when omitted, so an
51	 * empty configuration is a valid policy that never stops a step. A cap is
52	 * exceeded only when measured spend is strictly greater than its value, which
53	 * makes `0` an immediate stop and keeps an exactly-on-budget session running.
54	 */
55	export interface Config {
56	  /** Billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes) allowed in one session. */
57	  maxInputTokens?: number
58	  /** Output tokens allowed in one session. */
59	  maxOutputTokens?: number
60	  /** Input plus output tokens allowed in one session. */
61	  maxTotalTokens?: number
62	  /** Milliseconds the session log may span between its first and last event. */
63	  maxWallMs?: number
64	  /** EUR the priced routes of one session may cost; requires a non-empty {@link pricing}. */
65	  maxCostEur?: number
66	  /** EUR-per-million-token rates keyed by `provider/model`; a route absent here is never cost-capped. */
67	  pricing?: Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>
68	}
69	
70	/** Schemastery validation for {@link Config}. */
71	export const Config: z<Config> = z.object({
72	  maxInputTokens: z.number(),
73	  maxOutputTokens: z.number(),
74	  maxTotalTokens: z.number(),
75	  maxWallMs: z.number(),
76	  maxCostEur: z.number(),
77	  pricing: z.dict(z.object({
78	    inputEurPerMillionTokens: z.number().required(),
79	    outputEurPerMillionTokens: z.number().required(),
80	  })).default({}),
81	})

83	/** The caps a validated configuration actually enforces, paired with their values. */
84	interface ResolvedConfig {
85	  readonly caps: readonly (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[]
86	  readonly pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
87	  /** Whether {@link pricing} names any route; an empty table never reads the log. */
88	  readonly prices: boolean
89	  /** {@link pricingTableDigest} of {@link pricing}, computed once at load. */
90	  readonly pricingDigest: string
91	}
92	
93	/** Reject a cap that cannot express a ceiling before any session depends on it. */
94	function requireFiniteCap(cap: BudgetCapId, value: number): void {
95	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
96	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: ${cap} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
97	  }
98	}
99	
100	/** Reject a rate that cannot price a route before any session depends on it. */
101	function requireFiniteRate(route: string, field: keyof BudgetRoutePricing, value: number): void {
102	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
103	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: pricing["${route}"].${field} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
104	  }
105	}
106	
107	/**
108	 * Validate one deployment configuration and materialize the enforced caps.
109	 * Every rejection happens at plugin load, before a session can depend on a cap
110	 * the policy could not enforce.
111	 */
112	function resolveBudgetConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
113	  // The schema defaulted the table — the cast records that runtime fact.
114	  const pricing = config.pricing as Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
115	  for (const [route, rates] of Object.entries(pricing)) {
116	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'inputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens)
117	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'outputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens)
118	  }
119	  const prices = Object.keys(pricing).length > 0
120	  if (config.maxCostEur !== undefined && !prices) {
121	    throw new TypeError('budget-policy: maxCostEur needs a non-empty pricing table; an unpriced route has no cost cap')
122	  }
123	  const caps: (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[] = []
124	  for (const cap of BUDGET_CAP_ORDER) {
125	    const value = config[cap]
126	    if (value === undefined) continue
127	    requireFiniteCap(cap, value)
128	    caps.push([cap, value])
129	  }
130	  return { caps, pricing, prices, pricingDigest: pricingTableDigest(pricing) }
131	}
132	
133	/**
134	 * Build the durable price of one accounted message at the configured rates.
135	 * @param event - a message {@link unpricedUsage} selected, so its route is priced.
136	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
137	 * @returns the record to append for that step.
138	 */
139	function priceMessage(event: AccountedMessage, resolved: ResolvedConfig): UsagePriced {
140	  const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
141	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-non-null-assertion -- unpricedUsage yields only routes the table names
142	  const rates = resolved.pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]!
143	  const inputTokens = billedInputTokens(event.data.usage)
144	  const outputTokens = event.data.usage.outputTokens
145	  return {
146	    turn: event.data.turn,
147	    step: event.data.step,
148	    provider,
149	    model,
150	    inputTokens,
151	    outputTokens,
152	    inputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens,
153	    outputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens,
154	    costEur: costEurFor(inputTokens, outputTokens, rates),
155	    pricingDigest: resolved.pricingDigest,
156	  }
157	}
158	
159	/**
160	 * Record the price of every priced-route step the log does not price yet. The
161	 * selection is log-derived, so a resumed session prices what its predecessor
162	 * left unpriced and a second call over the same log appends nothing.
163	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log is priced.
164	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
165	 */
166	function priceUnpricedSteps(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): void {
167	  if (!resolved.prices) return
168	  for (const event of unpricedUsage(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)) {
169	    agent.session.append('usage/priced', priceMessage(event, resolved))
170	  }
171	}
172	
173	/**
174	 * Measure the session log against the caps this session actually runs under:
175	 * the configured caps tightened by the session's own `budget/caps` record.
176	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log carries the spend and its caps.
177	 * @param resolved - the caps and pricing this deployment enforces.
178	 * @returns the first breach in {@link BUDGET_CAP_ORDER}, or `undefined` while every cap holds.
179	 */
180	function detectBreach(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): BudgetBreach | undefined {
181	  const caps = tightenedCaps(resolved.caps, foldSessionCaps(agent.session.events))
182	  if (caps.length === 0) return undefined
183	  const spend = foldBudgetSpend(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)
184	  for (const [cap, limit] of caps) {
185	    const measured = measuredFor(spend, cap)
186	    if (measured > limit) return { cap, measured, limit }
187	  }
188	  return undefined
189	}
190	
191	/**
192	 * Block the session's goal so no goal-round driver continues it. The goal
193	 * domain is optional: a composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current
194	 * goal, or whose goal already left the `active` phase still gets the durable
195	 * breach record and the stopped turn.
196	 */
197	function blockGoal(ctx: Context, agent: Agent, breach: BudgetBreach): void {
198	  const goals = ctx.get('goals')
199	  if (goals === undefined) return
200	  const goal = goals.get(agent)
201	  if (goal === undefined || goal.phase !== 'active') return
202	  goals.block(agent, { id: goal.id, revision: goal.revision }, {
203	    code: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED,
204	    message: `Session budget ${breach.cap} exceeded: ${breach.measured} of ${breach.limit}.`,
205	  })
206	}
207	
208	/**
209	 * Register the pre-step budget check and the pricing records for the lifetime
210	 * of `ctx`.
211	 * @param ctx - plugin context; both listeners are disposed with it.
212	 * @param config - the per-session caps and pricing to enforce.
213	 * @throws {TypeError} when the configuration cannot express the caps it declares.
214	 */
215	export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
216	  const resolved = resolveBudgetConfig(config)
217	
218	  // Prepended so the budget decision precedes every listener that would build
219	  // request context or reserve continuation work for a step that cannot run.
220	  ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async ({ agent }, next): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {
221	    // Priced before the caps are read, so the last message before a breach is
222	    // priced by the same step that records the breach.
223	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
224	    const breach = detectBreach(agent, resolved)
225	    if (breach === undefined) return next()
226	    agent.session.append('budget/breach', breach)
227	    blockGoal(ctx, agent, breach)
228	    return { kind: 'reject' }
229	  }, { prepend: true })
230	
231	  // A turn that closes normally opens no further step, so its final message is
232	  // priced at the stop boundary instead.
233	  ctx.on('agent/turn-stopping', ({ agent }) => {
234	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
235	  })
236	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure budget vocabulary: the enforced cap names, the durable breach and
3	 * pricing payloads with their `SessionEventMap` declarations, the deployment
4	 * pricing entry, and the spend record the log fold produces. Kept free of
5	 * cordis, agent, and service imports so the fold, the plugin, and the
6	 * invariant companion share one home.
7	 *
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
9	 */
10	
11	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
13	
14	/** One enforced cap name; also the `Config` key that sets it. */
15	export type BudgetCapId =
16	  | 'maxInputTokens'
17	  | 'maxOutputTokens'
18	  | 'maxTotalTokens'
19	  | 'maxWallMs'
20	  | 'maxCostEur'
21	
22	/** EUR per one million tokens for one `provider/model` route. */
23	export interface BudgetRoutePricing {
24	  /** EUR per one million billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes). */
25	  readonly inputEurPerMillionTokens: number
26	  /** EUR per one million output tokens. */
27	  readonly outputEurPerMillionTokens: number
28	}
29	
30	/**
31	 * Session spend folded from the durable log. Token counts and cost cover every
32	 * `assistant/message` that carried provider `usage`; `wallMs` spans the log's
33	 * first and last event times, so it counts idle gaps between events but not
34	 * time elapsed since the newest event.
35	 */
36	export interface BudgetSpend {
37	  /** Billed input tokens: uncached input plus cache reads and writes. */
38	  readonly inputTokens: number
39	  /** Output tokens, reasoning output included as the provider reported it. */
40	  readonly outputTokens: number
41	  /** {@link inputTokens} plus {@link outputTokens}. */
42	  readonly totalTokens: number
43	  /** Milliseconds between the log's first and last event times; `0` for an empty log. */
44	  readonly wallMs: number
45	  /** EUR priced from the configured table; usage on an unpriced route adds nothing. */
46	  readonly costEur: number
47	}
48	
49	/**
50	 * Ceilings recorded on one session's own log. Every cap is optional; a cap the
51	 * record omits leaves the deployment's configured value in force.
52	 */
53	export interface BudgetCaps {
54	  /** Billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes) allowed in this session. */
55	  readonly maxInputTokens?: number
56	  /** Output tokens allowed in this session. */
57	  readonly maxOutputTokens?: number
58	  /** Input plus output tokens allowed in this session. */
59	  readonly maxTotalTokens?: number
60	  /** Milliseconds this session's log may span between its first and last event. */
61	  readonly maxWallMs?: number
62	  /** EUR this session's priced routes may cost; an unpriced route contributes nothing to it. */
63	  readonly maxCostEur?: number
64	}
65	
66	/** The durable record of one cap that stopped the next model request. */
67	export interface BudgetBreach {
68	  /** The cap that tripped. */
69	  readonly cap: BudgetCapId
70	  /** Spend measured from the log at the moment the step was stopped. */
71	  readonly measured: number
72	  /** The configured value {@link measured} exceeded. */
73	  readonly limit: number
74	}
75	
76	/**
77	 * One `assistant/message` event whose provider accounting is present. The
78	 * pricing helpers select and return this narrowed form, so a caller holding one
79	 * reads `usage` without repeating the presence check.
80	 */
81	export type AccountedMessage = SessionEvent<'assistant/message'> & { data: { usage: TokenUsage } }
82	
83	/** The durable price of one step, in the rates the configured table held. */
84	export interface UsagePriced {
85	  /** The turn that owned the priced step. */
86	  readonly turn: number
87	  /** The priced step within {@link turn}. */
88	  readonly step: number
89	  /** Provider of the route that served the step. */
90	  readonly provider: string
91	  /** Model of the route that served the step. */
92	  readonly model: string
93	  /** Billed input tokens: uncached input plus cache reads and writes. */
94	  readonly inputTokens: number
95	  /** Output tokens as the provider reported them. */
96	  readonly outputTokens: number
97	  /** EUR per one million billed input tokens applied to this step. */
98	  readonly inputEurPerMillionTokens: number
99	  /** EUR per one million output tokens applied to this step. */
100	  readonly outputEurPerMillionTokens: number
101	  /** EUR this step cost at the recorded rates. */
102	  readonly costEur: number
103	  /** Digest of the whole pricing table these rates came from. */
104	  readonly pricingDigest: string
105	}

107	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
108	  interface SessionEventMap {
109	    /**
110	     * Ceilings this one session runs under, recorded by whoever created it for
111	     * a narrower purpose than the deployment's own configuration. The caps the
112	     * policy enforces are the configured caps tightened by the latest record in
113	     * the log: a cap only this record carries applies as written, and a cap
114	     * both carry applies at the smaller of the two, so a record can never buy a
115	     * session more budget than its deployment configured.
116	     */
117	    'budget/caps': BudgetCaps
118	    /**
119	     * One configured session budget stopped the step that was about to make a
120	     * model request: the cap that tripped, the spend measured from the events
121	     * preceding this one, and the configured value that spend exceeded. The
122	     * step is rejected after this event, so the record is the only durable
123	     * explanation for a turn that ends without a model call.
124	     */
125	    'budget/breach': BudgetBreach
126	    /**
127	     * One `assistant/message` of a priced route — a `provider/model` the
128	     * configured pricing table names — priced at the rates that table held:
129	     * `costEur = (inputTokens * inputEurPerMillionTokens + outputTokens *
130	     * outputEurPerMillionTokens) / 1_000_000`, with `pricingDigest` naming the
131	     * table version those rates came from. A route the table does not name gets
132	     * no event, so cost per session replays from the log for exactly the steps
133	     * the deployment had priced when they ran.
134	     */
135	    'usage/priced': UsagePriced
136	  }
137	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure session-log folds behind every budget decision: the spend a cap is
3	 * measured against, and the steps whose price the log does not yet state. The
4	 * policy plugin and the invariant companion both read through them, so a
5	 * recorded breach or price is recomputable from the same events by anyone
6	 * holding the log.
7	 *
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
9	 */
10	
11	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
13	import { billedInputTokens, costEurFor, routeKey } from './pricing.ts'
14	import type { AccountedMessage, BudgetCapId, BudgetCaps, BudgetRoutePricing, BudgetSpend } from './types.ts'
15	
16	/**
17	 * Evaluation order of the caps. The first cap the log exceeds is the one
18	 * recorded, so this order decides which breach a session that overruns two
19	 * caps in the same step reports, and it is the order every enforced cap list
20	 * is rendered in.
21	 */
22	export const BUDGET_CAP_ORDER: readonly BudgetCapId[] = [
23	  'maxInputTokens',
24	  'maxOutputTokens',
25	  'maxTotalTokens',
26	  'maxWallMs',
27	  'maxCostEur',
28	]
29	
30	/** The key one step is identified by within its own session log. */
31	function stepKey(turn: number, step: number): string {
32	  return `${turn}/${step}`
33	}
34	
35	/** Whether one event is an assistant message the provider reported accounting for. */
36	function isAccounted(event: SessionEvent): event is AccountedMessage {
37	  return event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined
38	}
39	
40	/**
41	 * Fold billed spend and elapsed wall time out of one session log.
42	 *
43	 * Only `assistant/message` carries a step's final provider accounting, so it is
44	 * the single usage source: the earlier `assistant/chunk` usage sample for the
45	 * same step is deliberately ignored rather than counted twice. Each message
46	 * prices against its own `provider/model` provenance, so a route switch mid
47	 * session bills each step at the rate configured for the route that served it;
48	 * a route absent from `pricing` contributes tokens but no cost.
49	 *
50	 * @param events - the session events to fold, oldest first.
51	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
52	 * @returns the spend measured over exactly those events.
53	 */
54	export function foldBudgetSpend(
55	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
56	  pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>,
57	): BudgetSpend {
58	  let inputTokens = 0
59	  let outputTokens = 0
60	  let costEur = 0
61	  for (const event of events) {
62	    if (!isAccounted(event)) continue
63	    const input = billedInputTokens(event.data.usage)
64	    inputTokens += input
65	    outputTokens += event.data.usage.outputTokens
66	    const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
67	    const rates = pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]
68	    if (rates === undefined) continue
69	    costEur += costEurFor(input, event.data.usage.outputTokens, rates)
70	  }
71	  const first = events[0]
72	  const last = events[events.length - 1]
73	  return {
74	    inputTokens,
75	    outputTokens,
76	    totalTokens: inputTokens + outputTokens,
77	    wallMs: first === undefined || last === undefined ? 0 : last.time - first.time,
78	    costEur,
79	  }
80	}
81	
82	/**
83	 * Select the priced-route steps the log does not yet state a price for.
84	 *
85	 * The selection is a function of the log alone, so a resumed session prices
86	 * exactly the steps its predecessor left unpriced and never prices one twice: a
87	 * step is skipped once any `usage/priced` in the log carries its turn and step.
88	 * A message without provider accounting, and a message on a `provider/model`
89	 * the table does not name, are both skipped — an unpriced route has no rate to
90	 * record.
91	 *
92	 * @param events - the session events to read, oldest first.
93	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
94	 * @returns the messages awaiting a durable price, in log order.
95	 */
96	export function unpricedUsage(
97	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
98	  pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>,
99	): readonly AccountedMessage[] {
100	  const priced = new Set<string>()
101	  for (const event of events) {
102	    if (event.type !== 'usage/priced') continue
103	    priced.add(stepKey(event.data.turn, event.data.step))
104	  }
105	  const pending: AccountedMessage[] = []
106	  for (const event of events) {
107	    if (!isAccounted(event)) continue
108	    const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
109	    if (pricing[routeKey(provider, model)] === undefined) continue
110	    if (priced.has(stepKey(event.data.turn, event.data.step))) continue
111	    pending.push(event)
112	  }
113	  return pending
114	}
115	
116	/**
117	 * Read the ceilings one session's own log records for itself.
118	 *
119	 * Last-wins: a session that records its caps twice runs under the newest
120	 * record alone, which is what makes the caps a function of the log rather than
121	 * of the order a reader happens to visit the events in.
122	 *
123	 * @param events - the session events to read, oldest first.
124	 * @returns the latest recorded caps, empty when the log records none.
125	 */
126	export function foldSessionCaps(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): BudgetCaps {
127	  let caps: BudgetCaps = {}
128	  for (const event of events) {
129	    if (event.type === 'budget/caps') caps = event.data
130	  }
131	  return caps
132	}
133	
134	/**
135	 * Tighten the deployment's enforced caps by the ceilings one session recorded.
136	 *
137	 * A cap only the session records applies as written, and a cap both carry
138	 * applies at the smaller of the two, so a recorded ceiling can only ever narrow
139	 * what the deployment configured.
140	 *
141	 * @param configured - the deployment's enforced caps, in {@link BUDGET_CAP_ORDER}.
142	 * @param session - the caps the session's log records for itself.
143	 * @returns the caps to measure this session against, in {@link BUDGET_CAP_ORDER}.
144	 */
145	export function tightenedCaps(
146	  configured: readonly (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[],
147	  session: BudgetCaps,
148	): readonly (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[] {
149	  const byCap = new Map<BudgetCapId, number>(configured)
150	  for (const cap of BUDGET_CAP_ORDER) {
151	    const recorded = session[cap]
152	    if (recorded === undefined) continue
153	    const current = byCap.get(cap)
154	    byCap.set(cap, current === undefined ? recorded : Math.min(current, recorded))
155	  }
156	  return BUDGET_CAP_ORDER.flatMap((cap) => {
157	    const value = byCap.get(cap)
158	    return value === undefined ? [] : [[cap, value] as const]
159	  })
160	}
161	
162	/**
163	 * Read the spend one cap is measured against.
164	 * @param spend - folded session spend.

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	A durable spend ceiling for one session: configured token, wall-clock, and cost caps, tightened by whatever caps the session's own log records, are measured against that log before every proposed step, and the first cap the log exceeds records a `budget/breach` event, blocks the session's goal, and rejects the step so no further model request is made. Every step a priced route served also records a `usage/priced` event, so what a session cost is a durable fact rather than an in-memory total. Nothing is measured in memory — the caps read the same durable events a replay reads, so a recorded breach or price is reproducible by anyone holding the log. Decision record: [the budget-policy Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-budget-policy.md).
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: budget-policy
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
12	  config:
13	    maxInputTokens: 2000000      # billed input: uncached input + cache reads + cache writes
14	    maxOutputTokens: 400000      # output tokens, provider-reported
15	    maxTotalTokens: 2400000      # input + output
16	    maxWallMs: 3600000           # span between the log's first and last event
17	    maxCostEur: 25               # priced routes only; needs a non-empty pricing table
18	    pricing:
19	      deepseek/deepseek-chat:
20	        inputEurPerMillionTokens: 0.25
21	        outputEurPerMillionTokens: 1.0
22	```
23	
24	Every cap is optional and uncapped when omitted, so an empty configuration is a valid policy that never stops a step and never reads the log. A cap is exceeded only when measured spend is strictly greater than its value: `0` stops the session at the first recorded spend, and a session exactly on budget keeps running.
25	
26	Validation happens at plugin load, before any session can depend on a cap the policy could not enforce. A cap or rate that is not a finite non-negative number throws, and `maxCostEur` without a non-empty `pricing` table throws — an unpriced route has no cost cap, so a cost ceiling over an empty table would silently enforce nothing.
27	
28	`pricing` keys are `provider/model`, matching the provenance each assistant message carries. A route absent from the table contributes its tokens to the token caps but nothing to `costEur`, so token caps remain the enforcement of last resort for a route whose price the deployment has not stated.
29	
30	## Plugin contract (namespace: `budget-policy`)
31	
32	A function/namespace plugin (`name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply`), not a service. It injects `ctx.agents` and registers one prepended `agent/pre-step` listener and one `agent/turn-stopping` listener; `ctx.goals` is read optionally through `ctx.get('goals')`, so the policy enforces identically in a composition without the goal domain.
33	
34	The pre-step listener is prepended so the budget decision precedes every listener that would build request context or reserve continuation work for a step that cannot run. On a breach it does not call `next()`: the chain short-circuits and the loop closes the turn with reason `blocked`, having opened no step.
35	
36	`foldBudgetSpend(events, pricing)`, `measuredFor(spend, cap)`, `unpricedUsage(events, pricing)`, `foldSessionCaps(events)`, `tightenedCaps(configured, session)`, `BUDGET_CAP_ORDER`, and `pricingTableDigest(pricing)` are exported so a supervisor can recompute any recorded measurement, price, or enforced cap from the log.
37	
38	### Measuring spend from the log
39	
40	`assistant/message` is the single usage source: it carries a step's final provider accounting, so the earlier `assistant/chunk` usage sample for the same step is deliberately ignored rather than counted twice. A message without `usage` contributes nothing. Billed input is the disjoint sum of `inputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, and `cacheWriteTokens`; output is `outputTokens` as the provider reported it. Each message prices against its own `provider/model` provenance, so a route switch mid-session bills each step at the rate configured for the route that served it.
41	
42	`maxWallMs` measures the span between the log's first and last event times. It therefore counts idle gaps between events, including the gap across a process restart, but not time elapsed since the newest event — which is what makes the measurement a function of the log rather than of the clock at read time.
43	
44	### Per-session caps
45	
46	A session created for a narrower purpose than the whole deployment records its own ceilings as a `budget/caps` event carrying any subset of the five cap fields. The caps enforced for that session are the configured caps tightened by the latest `budget/caps` in its log: a cap only the record carries applies as written, a cap both carry applies at the smaller of the two, and a cap neither carries stays uncapped. A record can therefore only ever narrow what the deployment configured, which is what lets an orchestrator hand one session a slice of the deployment's budget without being able to grant it more.
47	
48	The caps are folded from the log like the spend they bound, so a resumed session enforces exactly the caps its own log records and the model sees nothing: `budget/caps` reaches no model request. A `maxCostEur` recorded on a session whose routes the `pricing` table does not name measures against a cost of zero and therefore never trips, exactly as a configured cost cap does over an unpriced route.
49	
50	### What a breach does
51	
52	1. Appends `budget/breach` with the cap that tripped, the measured spend, and the configured value it exceeded. The caps are evaluated in the fixed order `maxInputTokens`, `maxOutputTokens`, `maxTotalTokens`, `maxWallMs`, `maxCostEur`, and the first one exceeded is the one recorded.
53	2. Blocks a current `active` goal through `ctx.goals.block` with code `budget-exhausted` and the message `Session budget <cap> exceeded: <measured> of <limit>.` The block is durable and disarms continuation, so a goal-round driver does not resume the goal afterwards. A composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current goal, or whose goal already left `active` still gets the breach record and the stopped turn.
54	3. Returns `{ kind: 'reject' }`, which ends the turn without opening a step.
55	
56	Spend never decreases, so a later step in the same session breaches again: each stopped step records its own event, and the durable log states exactly how many attempts the exhausted budget turned away. Raising a cap and reloading the deployment is the way to resume.
57	
58	### What a priced step records
59	
60	`usage/priced` states the price of one `assistant/message` whose `provider/model` the `pricing` table names: the `turn` and `step` it prices, that route's `provider` and `model`, the `inputTokens` (billed input) and `outputTokens` it charges for, the `inputEurPerMillionTokens` and `outputEurPerMillionTokens` applied, the resulting `costEur = (inputTokens * inputEurPerMillionTokens + outputTokens * outputEurPerMillionTokens) / 1_000_000`, and a `pricingDigest`. The digest is the lowercase SHA-256 of the whole configured table — route keys ordered by code unit, each entry serialized as its input rate then its output rate — so a reader can tell which table version priced a step and one changed rate changes the digest. Rates travel in the record itself, which is what makes session cost replayable without the deployment configuration. A route the table does not name records nothing.
61	
62	Which steps to price is read from the log, not remembered: a step is priced when its message carries `usage`, its route is priced, and no `usage/priced` in the log already carries its turn and step. A resumed session therefore prices exactly what its predecessor left unpriced, and never prices a step twice. The records are written at two points — inside the pre-step listener, before the caps are read, so the last message before a breach is priced by the same step that records the breach; and at `agent/turn-stopping`, so the final step of a turn that closes normally is priced too.
63	
64	A turn that ends by error or abort reaches neither point, so its last message stays unpriced until the session's next pre-step or stop boundary; a session abandoned in that state keeps one unpriced step in its log.
65	
66	### Invariant companion
67	
68	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy/invariant` recomputes each durable record independently. A breach's recorded `measured` must exceed `limit`, and for the log-derived caps it must equal this package's fold over exactly the events preceding the record; `maxCostEur` depends on the deployment pricing table, which the log does not carry, so a cost breach is checked only for the exceeded-its-limit relation. A price must cite an earlier `assistant/message` with the same turn and step whose billed tokens and route it reproduces exactly, its `costEur` must equal its own rates applied to its own tokens, and no earlier `usage/priced` may carry the same turn and step.
69	
70	A `budget/caps` record may only tighten. The deployment's configured caps are not in the log, so the companion compares each cap against the caps the same session's earlier `budget/caps` records already fold to: raising one of those, or dropping it so the cap disappears, is rejected at append. Widening a cap the deployment configured is outside what the log can show and is refused by the enforcing fold instead, which never takes a recorded value above the configured one.
71	
72	## Model Experience
73	
74	### Stopped step
75	
76	#### What the model sees
77	
78	Nothing. A breach is decided before the step opens, so no prompt section, tool schema, tool result, or message text is added, and no model request is made for the stopped step or for any later step while the cap holds. The breach record, the pricing records, and the goal's `budget-exhausted` block reason are durable state for humans and supervising processes; none of them is a surface event, so none reaches a model request.
79	
80	#### Token effect
81	
82	Zero added tokens, and the request the stopped step would have sent is never spent.
83	
84	#### KV Cache effect
85	
86	Independent: the request surface is neither extended nor rewritten, so an already-reusable prefix stays reusable; the session simply issues no further request while the cap holds.
87	
88	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
89	
90	- **Session-scoped only** — the caps measure one session log. A deployment that wants a per-workspace, per-user, or per-day ceiling has no aggregation point here; subagent sessions carry their own logs and their own independent budgets.
91	- **Cost covers priced routes only** — usage on a `provider/model` absent from `pricing` adds tokens but no cost and records no `usage/priced`, so `maxCostEur` cannot be the sole ceiling for a deployment whose routes are not all priced, and an unpriced session has no cost the log can state.
92	- **A turn that ends by error or abort leaves its last step unpriced** — pricing happens at the next pre-step or at the normal stop boundary, and neither is reached when a turn fails or is cancelled. The record lands at the session's next pre-step or stop; a session abandoned right after such a turn keeps one unpriced step.
93	- **One input rate per route** — the table prices billed input with a single number, so a provider that discounts cache reads against cache misses is priced at the uncached rate.
94	- **No warning before the stop** — the policy has no advisory threshold that tells the model to wrap up before the cap trips; the first model-visible consequence of an exhausted budget is that the turn ends.
95	- **Raising a cap needs a reload** — configured caps are load-time configuration, so an exhausted session resumes only after the deployment is reconfigured and reloaded; a `budget/caps` record can only tighten, so there is no runtime grant either.
96	- **No session-cap authority** — any writer of a session's log can record `budget/caps`, and the record is honoured because it can only narrow. Nothing states which orchestrator owns a session's caps, so two writers on one session simply compose by last-wins-then-tighten.

434	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
435	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
436	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted

439	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
440	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
441	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
442	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
443	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
444	  const marker = '\n…'
445	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
446	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
447	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
448	}

450	/** How one command ended, as the evidence states it. */
451	function exitLine(result: ShellRunResult): string {
452	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
453	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
454	  return `${exit}${cause}`
455	}

459	  const lines: string[] = []
460	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
461	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
462	  return lines
463	}

465	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
466	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
467	  return bound([exitLine(result), ...outputLines(result)].join('\n'), maxChars)

504	function casedEvidenceOf(run: CasedCheckRun, named: readonly CaseFailure[], maxChars: number): string {

513	/**
514	 * Whether one captured stream disagrees with its expected digest. A truncated
515	 * stream disagrees whatever it holds: the executor dropped bytes the digest
516	 * covers, so the comparison cannot be made.
517	 */
518	function streamMismatch(
519	  stream: ShellRunResult['stdout'],
520	  expected: string | undefined,
521	  normalizers: readonly CheckCaseNormalizer[],
522	): boolean {
523	  return stream.truncated || caseChannelDigest(Buffer.from(stream.text, 'utf8'), normalizers) !== expected

526	/**
527	 * The configured channels of one case whose observed value disagrees with the
528	 * case's expected digest, in the canonical channel order the log records.
529	 * @param body - the case that ran.
530	 * @param result - what the candidate produced.
531	 * @param scope - the absolute `treeScope` directory, absent for a check that declares none.
532	 * @returns the mismatching channels; empty when the case passed.
533	 */
534	async function caseMismatches(
535	  body: CheckCase,
536	  result: ShellRunResult,
537	  scope: string | undefined,
538	): Promise<CheckCaseChannel[]> {
539	  const { normalizers } = body.comparator
540	  const mismatched = new Set<CheckCaseChannel>()
541	  for (const channel of body.comparator.channels) {
542	    switch (channel) {
543	      case 'exit':
544	        if (result.exitCode !== body.expected.exitCode) mismatched.add(channel)
545	        break
546	      case 'stdout':
547	        if (streamMismatch(result.stdout, body.expected.stdoutSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
548	        break
549	      case 'stderr':
550	        if (streamMismatch(result.stderr, body.expected.stderrSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
551	        break
552	      case 'tree':
553	        // Authoring requires a treeScope for every check whose cases compare the tree.
554	        if (await hashWorkspaceTree(scope as string, normalizers) !== body.expected.treeSha256) mismatched.add(channel)
555	        break
556	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
557	      default:
558	        return assertNever(channel)
559	    }
560	  }
561	  return CHECK_CASE_CHANNELS.filter(channel => mismatched.has(channel))
562	}

588	/**
589	 * Run one case and capture all four channels: empty the case's `treeScope`,
590	 * stage its files, append its `argv` to the command, and feed its `stdin`.
591	 * Both executors of a case go through here — the runner measuring a candidate
592	 * and the instrument recording a reference — so what a case means is one
593	 * procedure rather than two that can drift.
594	 * @param shell - the composed shell executor.
595	 * @param execution - the resolved command, workspace, input, and bounds.
596	 * @returns the command's result and the tree scope it left.
597	 */
598	export async function captureCase(shell: Context['shell'], execution: CaseExecution): Promise<CaseCapture> {
599	  const scope = execution.treeScope === undefined ? undefined : join(execution.workspace, execution.treeScope)
600	  if (scope !== undefined) {
601	    await rm(scope, { recursive: true, force: true })
602	    await mkdir(scope, { recursive: true })
603	  }
604	  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(execution.input.files ?? {})) {
605	    const staged = join(execution.workspace, path)
606	    await mkdir(dirname(staged), { recursive: true })
607	    await writeFile(staged, content)
608	  }
609	  const stdin = execution.input.stdin
610	  const result = await shell.run(shell.resolve({
611	    command: [execution.command, ...execution.input.argv].join(' '),
612	    workdir: execution.workspace,
613	    timeoutMs: execution.timeoutMs,
614	    signal: execution.signal,
615	    ...stdin === undefined ? {} : { stdin },
616	  }))
617	  return { result, ...scope === undefined ? {} : { scope } }
618	}

620	/**
621	 * The expected digests one capture establishes for a comparator's configured
622	 * channels, which is what {@link caseMismatches} later compares a candidate
623	 * against. A truncated compared stream yields no digest for that channel: the
624	 * executor dropped bytes the digest would cover, so nothing could ever match it.
625	 * @param capture - what the reference produced for the case.
626	 * @param comparator - the channels compared and the normalizers applied first.
627	 * @returns the expectation, holding one value per configured channel that could be digested.
628	 */
629	export async function caseExpectation(
630	  capture: CaseCapture,
631	  comparator: CheckCaseComparator,
632	): Promise<CheckCaseExpectation> {
633	  const { normalizers } = comparator
634	  const { result } = capture
635	  const digest = (stream: ShellRunResult['stdout']): Record<string, never> | { sha256: string } => (
636	    stream.truncated ? {} : { sha256: caseChannelDigest(Buffer.from(stream.text, 'utf8'), normalizers) }
637	  )
638	  let expectation: CheckCaseExpectation = {}
639	  for (const channel of comparator.channels) {
640	    switch (channel) {
641	      case 'exit':
642	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...result.exitCode === null ? {} : { exitCode: result.exitCode } }
643	        break
644	      case 'stdout': {
645	        const value = digest(result.stdout)
646	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...'sha256' in value ? { stdoutSha256: value.sha256 } : {} }
647	        break
648	      }
649	      case 'stderr': {
650	        const value = digest(result.stderr)
651	        expectation = { ...expectation, ...'sha256' in value ? { stderrSha256: value.sha256 } : {} }
652	        break
653	      }
654	      case 'tree':
655	        // Only a comparator naming `tree` reaches here, and such a case is
656	        // executed with the scope its check declares.
657	        expectation = { ...expectation, treeSha256: await hashWorkspaceTree(capture.scope as string, normalizers) }
658	        break
659	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
660	      default:
661	        return assertNever(channel)
662	    }
663	  }
664	  return expectation
665	}

667	/** One rendered cluster with the check facts its line names. */
668	interface RenderedCluster extends DirectiveCluster {
669	  readonly outcome: string
670	  readonly total: number
671	  readonly weightTotal: number
672	  readonly exitClass: CaseExitClass
673	}

675	/** Group one cased check's failed cases by the channels that disagreed and how the candidate ended. */
676	function clustersOf(check: StandardCheck, result: CheckResult): RenderedCluster[] {
677	  const cases = result.cases
678	  /* v8 ignore next -- only a cased result reaches here, and a cased result carries its tally */
679	  if (cases === undefined) return []
680	  const clusters = new Map<string, RenderedCluster>()
681	  for (const failed of cases.failed) {
682	    const key = `${failed.exitClass}|${failed.channels.join(',')}`
683	    const existing = clusters.get(key)
684	    clusters.set(key, {
685	      checkId: result.checkId,
686	      channels: failed.channels,
687	      count: (existing?.count ?? 0) + 1,
688	      weight: (existing?.weight ?? 0) + failed.weight,
689	      outcome: check.outcome,
690	      total: cases.total,
691	      weightTotal: cases.weightTotal,
692	      exitClass: failed.exitClass,
693	    })
694	  }
695	  return [...clusters.values()]
696	}

698	/**
699	 * One directive per failed run. A cased check contributes one line per failure
700	 * cluster, naming its authored outcome, the cluster's count and weight, the
701	 * channels that disagreed, and how the candidate ended — never a case body, an
702	 * expected digest, or a byte of captured output. A check without cases
703	 * contributes its recorded evidence line.
704	 * @param failures - the run's failing results, in check order.
705	 * @param checks - the standard's active checks, supplying each outcome text.
706	 * @param maxChars - bound of the rendered detail.
707	 * @returns the directive, carrying `clusters` when a cased check failed.
708	 */
709	function describeFailures(
710	  failures: readonly CheckResult[],
711	  checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
712	  maxChars: number,
713	): DirectiveRequest {
714	  const lines: string[] = []
715	  const clusters: DirectiveCluster[] = []
716	  for (const failure of failures) {
717	    const check = checks.find(candidate => candidate.id === failure.checkId)
718	    if (check === undefined || failure.cases === undefined) {
719	      lines.push(failure.evidence)
720	      continue
721	    }
722	    for (const cluster of clustersOf(check, failure)) {
723	      clusters.push({ checkId: cluster.checkId, channels: cluster.channels, count: cluster.count, weight: cluster.weight })
724	      lines.push(`${cluster.outcome}: ${cluster.count} of ${cluster.total} cases failed (weight ${cluster.weight} of ${cluster.weightTotal}); mismatching channels: ${cluster.channels.join(', ')}; ${EXIT_PHRASE[cluster.exitClass]}`)
725	    }
726	  }
727	  return {
728	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
729	    detail: bound(lines.map((line, index) => `${index + 1}. ${line}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
730	    ...clusters.length === 0 ? {} : { clusters },
731	  }
732	}

763	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
764	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
765	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
766	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
767	  ))
768	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
769	  const total: TokenUsage = {
770	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
771	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
772	  }
773	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
774	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
775	      const value = step[key]
776	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
777	    })
778	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
779	  }
780	  return total

910	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
911	  private async drive(
912	    agent: Agent,
913	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
914	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
915	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
916	    implementer: RunImplementer,
917	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
918	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
919	    await agent.whenIdle()
920	    const runDirectory = await this.reserve(agent, definition)
921	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
922	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
923	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
924	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
925	    })
926	    goals.disarm(agent)
927	    const authored = completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
928	    // Authorship validated every case against the reference it carries and kept
929	    // the reference alone; the bodies stay here, for the reservation and the
930	    // per-case execution.
931	    const bodies = new Map(definition.checks.flatMap(check => (
932	      check.caseBodies === undefined ? [] : [[check.id, check.caseBodies] as const]
933	    )))
934	    const immutable = definition.task.immutable ?? []
935	    // Stock the reservation and digest the check-owned set before the
936	    // implementer's first turn: that digest is what every later attempt is
937	    // compared against.
938	    await materializeChecks(runDirectory, authored, bodies)
939	    let checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
940	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
941	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
942	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
943	    try {
944	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
945	        await this.implement(agent, implementer, prompt, attempt, request.signal)
946	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
947	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
948	        if (await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable) !== checkOwned) {
949	          attempts.push(await this.recordTamper(agent, implementer, standard, ref, request.workspace, attempt))
950	          break
951	        }
952	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task)
953	        const scripts = await materializeChecks(runDirectory, standard, bodies)
954	        // The validator just rewrote its own directory, so the set it now owns
955	        // is the baseline the next attempt must still find.
956	        checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
957	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts, bodies)
958	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
959	          executor: 'runner',
960	          treeHash,
961	        })
962	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
963	        if (outcome.certified) {
964	          certificate = outcome.certificate
965	          const current = goals.get(agent)
966	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
967	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
968	          }
969	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
970	          break
971	        }
972	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, standard.checks, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
973	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
974	        prompt = followupText(directive)
975	      }
976	    } finally {
977	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
978	    }
979	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
980	    return {
981	      environment: definition.id,
982	      sessionId: agent.id,
983	      stamp,
984	      attempts,
985	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
986	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
987	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
988	    }
989	  }

1178	  /**

1180	   * workspace. A reserved check runs its script; an unreserved one runs its
1181	   * instruction inline. A check that carries cases runs once per case and its
1182	   * verdict follows the cases; every other check's verdict is its exit code.
1183	   */
1184	  private async execute(
1185	    checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
1186	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
1187	    scripts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
1188	    bodies: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly CheckCase[]>,
1189	  ): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
1190	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
1191	    for (const check of checks) {
1192	      const script = scripts.get(check.id)
1193	      const command = script === undefined ? check.run : `. ${script}`
1194	      const cases = bodies.get(check.id)
1195	      if (cases === undefined) {
1196	        const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(this.checkSpec(command, request))

1198	          checkId: check.id,
1199	          status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
1200	          evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
1201	        })

1203	      }
1204	      const run = await this.executeCases(check, cases, command, request)

1214	          total: run.total,

1218	            id: failure.id,
1219	            weight: failure.weight,
1220	            channels: failure.channels,

1243	  private async executeCases(
1244	    check: StandardCheck,
1245	    cases: readonly CheckCase[],
1246	    command: string,
1247	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
1248	  ): Promise<CasedCheckRun> {

1266	      }

1270	      passed: passedCases,
1271	      total: cases.length,
1272	      weightPassed,

109	/** Experiments (`ctx.experiments`): a frozen, paired, budgeted comparison of two arms. */
110	export class ExperimentService extends Service {
111	  static inject = ['environments', 'fleet']
112	
113	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
114	    bootstrapResamples: z.natural().min(1).default(1000),
115	    confidenceLevel: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.95),
116	    minimumDelta: z.number().default(0),
117	    cellTokenCap: z.natural().min(1).required(),
118	    tokenBudget: z.natural().min(1).required(),
119	  })

121	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig

123	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
124	    super(ctx, 'experiments')
125	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
126	  }

128	  /**
129	   * Freeze a plan, run both arms through the fleet at the same repetition
130	   * indexes, and fold the paired comparison. Every refusal happens before the
131	   * first cell runs; a cell the fleet kept as an error leaves its repetition
132	   * unpaired instead of failing the experiment.
133	   * @param plan - environments, repetitions, the two arms with their model
134	   *   routes and optional implementers, the workspace root, and an optional
135	   *   policy version, base seed, frozen digest, abort signal, and result sink.
136	   * @returns the digest, both arms with their stamp groups, one cell per
137	   *   environment, the pooled delta with its interval, the spend, and the verdict.
138	   * @throws {@link ExperimentError} for a plan that names no or a duplicate or
139	   *   unregistered environment, asks for no repetition, sets a seed that is not
140	   *   a safe non-negative integer, declares a digest its content does not
141	   *   freeze to, or projects more tokens than the budget.
142	   */
143	  async run(plan: ExperimentPlan): Promise<ExperimentResult> {
144	    const digest = this.freeze(plan)
145	    const arms: ExperimentArms = {
146	      baseline: resolveArm(plan.baseline, digest, 'baseline'),
147	      candidate: resolveArm(plan.candidate, digest, 'candidate'),
148	    }
149	    const baseline = await this.runArm(plan, arms.baseline)
150	    const candidate = await this.runArm(plan, arms.candidate)
151	    const result = foldExperiment({
152	      digest,
153	      arms,
154	      environments: plan.environments,
155	      repetitions: plan.repetitions,
156	      thresholds: this.resolved.thresholds,
157	      baseline,
158	      candidate,
159	    })
160	    await record(result, plan.sink)
161	    return result
162	  }
163	
164	  /** Validate the plan, compute its digest, and check the projection against the budget. */
165	  private freeze(plan: ExperimentPlan): string {
166	    if (!Number.isInteger(plan.repetitions) || plan.repetitions < 1) {
167	      throw new ExperimentError(`repetitions must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.repetitions)}`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
168	    }
169	    if (plan.seed !== undefined && !isSeed(plan.seed)) {
170	      throw new ExperimentError(`seed must be a non-negative integer, got ${String(plan.seed)}`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
171	    }
172	    if (plan.environments.length === 0) throw new ExperimentError('the plan names no environment', 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
173	    const named = new Set<EnvironmentId>()
174	    for (const environment of plan.environments) {
175	      if (named.has(environment)) throw new ExperimentError(`environment "${environment}" is named twice`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
176	      if (this.ctx.environments.get(environment) === undefined) {
177	        throw new ExperimentError(`environment "${environment}" is not registered`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
178	      }
179	      named.add(environment)
180	    }
181	    const digest = planDigest(plan, this.resolved.thresholds)
182	    if (plan.digest !== undefined && plan.digest !== digest) {
183	      throw new ExperimentError(`the plan declares digest ${plan.digest} but freezes to ${digest}`, 'EXPERIMENT_PLAN_NOT_FROZEN')
184	    }
185	    const projected = projectedTokens(plan, this.resolved.thresholds.cellTokenCap)
186	    if (projected > this.resolved.tokenBudget) {
187	      throw new ExperimentError(`the plan projects ${projected} tokens over a budget of ${this.resolved.tokenBudget}`, 'EXPERIMENT_OVER_BUDGET')
188	    }
189	    return digest
190	  }
191	
192	  /** Run one arm as one fleet run over the plan's environments under the arm's group. */
193	  private async runArm(plan: ExperimentPlan, arm: ExperimentArm): Promise<FleetRunReport> {
194	    return this.ctx.fleet.run({
195	      environments: { ids: plan.environments },
196	      models: [arm.model],
197	      implementer: arm.implementer,
198	      repetitions: plan.repetitions,
199	      workspaceRoot: plan.workspaceRoot,
200	      group: arm.group,
201	      ...plan.policyVersion === undefined ? {} : { policyVersion: plan.policyVersion },
202	      ...plan.seed === undefined ? {} : { seed: plan.seed },
203	      ...plan.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: plan.signal },
204	    })
205	  }
206	}

213	 * @param role - which arm of the comparison this is.
214	 * @returns the arm the fleet call and the result both state.
215	 */
216	function resolveArm(arm: ExperimentArmPlan, digest: string, role: ExperimentArmRole): ExperimentArm {

1	/**
2	 * Freezing one experiment plan: the content digest computed before any cell
3	 * runs, and the stamp `group` each arm's sessions carry so a later fold can
4	 * find them in the logs.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments/plan
7	 */
8	
9	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
10	import type { EnvironmentRunImplementer } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
11	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { ExperimentArmPlan, ExperimentArmRole, ExperimentPlan, ExperimentThresholds } from './types.ts'
13	
14	/**
15	 * Group namespace this package owns. A `group` starting with it names an
16	 * experiment arm, so no other producer may mint one.
17	 */
18	export const EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX = 'experiment-'
19	
20	/** Self-declared version of the digested plan fields; a change to what they cover changes it. */
21	const EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION = 3
22	
23	/** Arm roles in the order the digest and the runs take them. */
24	export const EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES: readonly ExperimentArmRole[] = ['baseline', 'candidate']
25	
26	const GROUP_PATTERN = new RegExp(`^${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}([0-9a-f]{64})-(${EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.join('|')})$`)
27	
28	/**
29	 * The implementer one arm runs under.
30	 * @param arm - one arm as the plan names it.
31	 * @returns the named implementer, or the arm's own model route when it names none.
32	 */
33	export function armImplementer(arm: ExperimentArmPlan): EnvironmentRunImplementer {
34	  return arm.implementer ?? { kind: 'route' }
35	}
36	
37	/**
38	 * One implementer as the digest takes it: the discriminant, the subagent
39	 * provider, and its label, each in a fixed position, so the key order a caller
40	 * happened to write cannot change the digest.
41	 */
42	function digestedImplementer(implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer): readonly (string | null)[] {
43	  switch (implementer.kind) {
44	    case 'route':
45	      return [implementer.kind, null, null]
46	    case 'subagent':
47	      return [implementer.kind, implementer.provider, implementer.label ?? null]
48	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- EnvironmentRunImplementer is closed and every member is handled above */
49	    default:
50	      return assertNever(implementer, 'arm implementer')
51	  }
52	}
53	
54	/**
55	 * Content digest of the fields that decide what an experiment measures: the
56	 * two arms in role order, each with its model route and its implementer, the
57	 * environment ids sorted so a caller's listing order cannot change the
58	 * identity, the repetition count, the policy version and base seed both arms
59	 * ran under, and the thresholds. The deployment's token budget is deliberately
60	 * absent: it bounds what a deployment pays for, not what the comparison
61	 * measures. The policy version and the seed are present because both arms'
62	 * sessions are found in the logs by the groups this digest mints, so two
63	 * comparisons that differ in either must not collide on one group.
64	 * @param plan - the arms, environments, repetitions, policy version, and seed to freeze.
65	 * @param thresholds - the resolved statistical choices to freeze with them.
66	 * @returns the SHA-256 hex digest; identical inputs give identical digests.
67	 */
68	export function planDigest(plan: ExperimentPlan, thresholds: ExperimentThresholds): string {
69	  const content = JSON.stringify({
70	    version: EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION,
71	    arms: EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.map(role => [
72	      role,
73	      plan[role].provider,
74	      plan[role].model,
75	      digestedImplementer(armImplementer(plan[role])),
76	    ]),
77	    environments: [...plan.environments].sort(),
78	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
79	    policyVersion: plan.policyVersion ?? null,
80	    seed: plan.seed ?? null,
81	    thresholds: [
82	      thresholds.bootstrapResamples,
83	      thresholds.confidenceLevel,
84	      thresholds.minimumDelta,
85	      thresholds.cellTokenCap,
86	    ],
87	  })
88	  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * Stamp `group` one arm's sessions carry.
93	 * @param digest - the frozen plan digest.
94	 * @param role - which arm the group names.
95	 * @returns `experiment-<digest>-<role>`.
96	 */
97	export function experimentGroup(digest: string, role: ExperimentArmRole): string {
98	  return `${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}${digest}-${role}`
99	}
100	
101	/**
102	 * Read a group minted by {@link experimentGroup}.
103	 * @param group - a stamp group from an `environment/run` event.
104	 * @returns the digest and role, or `undefined` for a group outside this package's namespace or malformed inside it.
105	 */
106	export function parseExperimentGroup(group: string): { digest: string; role: ExperimentArmRole } | undefined {
107	  const match = GROUP_PATTERN.exec(group)
108	  if (match === null) return undefined
109	  return { digest: match[1] as string, role: match[2] as ExperimentArmRole }
110	}
111	
112	/**
113	 * Tokens a plan may spend at its per-cell cap: every environment, every
114	 * repetition, on both arms.
115	 * @param plan - the environments and repetitions to project.
116	 * @param cellTokenCap - tokens one cell may spend.
117	 * @returns the projected ceiling the token budget is checked against.
118	 */
119	export function projectedTokens(plan: ExperimentPlan, cellTokenCap: number): number {
120	  return plan.environments.length * plan.repetitions * EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.length * cellTokenCap
121	}

87	  /** Implementer every cell of this arm ran under, with the plan's default applied, so a stored result tells the arms apart alone. */
88	  readonly implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer
89	  /** `experiment-<digest>-<role>`, written into the `environment/run` stamp of every session of this arm. */
90	  readonly group: string

95	  readonly baseline: ExperimentArm
96	  readonly candidate: ExperimentArm

102	  readonly upper: number

105	/**
106	 * One environment's paired comparison. Every rate, mean, and delta covers the
107	 * paired repetitions alone, so a repetition an arm failed to report changes
108	 * `pairs` and `unpaired` rather than silently shifting a rate.
109	 */
110	export interface ExperimentCell {
111	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
112	  /** Repetition indexes both arms reported. */
113	  readonly pairs: number
114	  /** Repetition indexes that did not pair because an arm produced no report. */
115	  readonly unpaired: number
116	  /** Certified fraction of the baseline arm over the paired repetitions, `0` without pairs. */
117	  readonly baselineRate: number
118	  /** Certified fraction of the candidate arm over the paired repetitions, `0` without pairs. */
119	  readonly candidateRate: number

132	/** Model usage summed over every reported cell of both arms, paired or not. */
